chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The two parties in a transaction have the option (to cancel) until they separate, and the owner of the animal has three days.' I said: 'A man buys goods from another man, then leaves them with him and says, 'Bring us the price.'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he comes within the time between then and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The option/right to choose to cancel or confirm
key_terms.فِيمَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَ: Within the time between then and three days

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cancelling a sale deal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'Khiyar al-Majlis' (option of the session), granting both parties the right to rescind a contract until they physically part ways, while extending a three-day examination period specifically for livestock. It further clarifies a nuanced commercial scenario where goods are retained pending payment, establishing that the transaction remains valid if payment occurs within three days, thereby preventing arbitrary cancellation. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness and clarity in trade, ensuring that neither party is bound by uncertainty or delay.
